convoLines.text: "You look handy. What did you do with your hands, before?"
"Useful. Everything useful matters now. I mean that as a compliment. I'm sure it'll be fine."
"Come, sit — Still on what you did with your hands."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
Tyler has been stockpiling where nobody looks. "Take half. You've got the hands for it." (+4 wood, +4 fiber to the village stash.)
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Emma always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
You show them Yarrow — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Sleep's gone strange. I save the best bite for last at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What do you miss most? From before."
"God. Yes. I dream about soup. Actual soup, with a spoon."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Heh. Still on what you miss most."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"I should go. Before I overthink this conversation too."
The silence stretches a beat too long. They study their hands.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Right. Well." That's the whole goodbye.
"Is there someone here you don't trust? Be honest."
Their eyes flick, just for a second, toward the fire. "Noted. I'll watch too."
"Quick version — Still on who you don't trust."
"I don't know you well enough for that. Ask me again when we've survived something together."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
Sam looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Gotta run. Literally. Bye!"
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Got a read on anyone here yet? Who should I be watching?"
"Same. But keep your eyes open — some people here are performing, not surviving."
"Still on your read on people here."
"I don't know you well enough for that. Ask me again when we've survived something together."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to understand what happened. It's safer if people don't know. Please don't tell the others."
"That again?" Raj sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Alright — carefully, now. Both of us."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.'"
"The fire feels smaller without Emma. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on what's been happening."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Nancy grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Tyler is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
You show them Pawpaw — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"You missed a real hot meal. Soup, you said — with a spoon. Any of that turn up?"
Nancy has an edge today — something curdled.
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Nancy rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"We went over this," Nancy says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Tyler nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
You show them Pawpaw — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Has this changed you? Like, fundamentally?"
They nod. "Okay."
"I should go. You know where to find me."

"This was good." They mean it.
"We gave them a good burial. Doesn't feel like enough, does it? ...sorry."

"I buried this before the Scattering. Seemed stupid to keep it secret." Marcus digs up a wrapped bundle — food, still good. (+1706 kcal to the pantry.)
"This one — Wild Soybean. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"This one — Feral Paddy Rice. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."

"You're kind. Don't let this place change that. That's the truth of it."

"I have opinions about the name. I am saving them for when they count."

"Sure. I'll be around."

"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. Meet me at the ridge above the creek and we'll fill packs before dark."

lines: d10: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Emma Kraemer is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d10: 🕯️ Emma Kraemer is dead — starvation. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d10: What Emma kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d10: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Ruth blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.

d10: 📖 LEARNED: Diplomatic Incident (Level 1). Trust builds 2x faster. You're TOO good though — once per week you can start a diplomatic incident: villagers argue, you pick the winner (+trust with them, -trust with the loser).
d10: 📖 LEARNED: Research & Records (Level 1). Find information fast: indexes, archives, and asking the right question.
d10: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d10: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Emma Kraemer, 10 days. The mantle passes to Ruth Goldstein.
d10: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Ruth Goldstein, 71 — a librarian. Her hands know different work now: Beast-calm.
d10: The fire knew Ruth — solid ground, earned at this fire.
d52: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Ruth Goldstein is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d52: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d52: 🕯️ Ruth Goldstein is dead — the arena. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d52: What Ruth kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d52: "Ruth's gone." Tancredi looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Ruth." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d52: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Owen blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d52: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Tracks (Level 1). Fresh tracks have sharp edges. Old tracks crumble. You can tell how recently something passed.
d52: 📖 LEARNED: Patient Aim (Level 1). One shot. You don't take the shot unless it's the shot.
d52: 📖 LEARNED: Animal Behavior (Level 1). Most animals flee. Give them an escape route and they take it. Cornered animals fight.
d52: 📖 LEARNED: Wire Snares (Level 1). A loop of wire on a game trail. Simple, effective, ancient. Check at dawn.

d52: 📖 LEARNED: Come Get Some (Level 1). Make exactly the right noise and the blind thing comes to investigate. Goad a blinded monster within 3 tiles: it lurches toward the sound on its next move. Stand where you want it.
d52: 📖 LEARNED: Scarecrow (Level 1). You can stage a fake injury to lure monsters into traps. They fall for it. Every time.
d52: 📖 LEARNED: Soft Step (Level 1). Move through woods like weather. Less noise, fewer surprises.
d52: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d52: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Ruth Goldstein, 52 days. The mantle passes to Owen Smith.
d52: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Owen Smith, 33 — a hunting guide. His hands know different work now: Beast-calm, Echo Location.
d52: The village's quarrel was with Ruth — and Ruth is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d52: At the grave, Tancredi, Raj, Elif and 1 more speak for Owen — "Ruth trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d52: The fire knew Owen before the Codex did — his name already carried weight here.
d59: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Owen Smith is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d59: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d59: 🕯️ Owen Smith is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d59: What Owen kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d59: "Owen's gone." Tancredi looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Owen." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d59: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Caleb blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d59: 📖 LEARNED: Fire in Rain (Level 1). Split wood — the inside is dry even when the outside is soaked. Feather sticks catch fast.
d59: 📖 LEARNED: Managing Fear (Level 1). Fear is data, not orders. Acknowledge it, then decide anyway. Courage is fear that kept going.

d59: 📖 LEARNED: Draw Fire (Level 1). In the wilds, beside your people, you make yourself the problem. Shout, wave, bleed loudly — the beast's eye stays on you and off them. Monsters focus you instead of your allies.

d59: 📖 LEARNED: Rally (Level 1). In the wilds, when the fight is lost and running would be sane, you look at the people standing with you and you do not run. Once per fight, when the trajectory turns hopeless and an ally stands beside you, you hold the line instead of fleeing. Not volume — a promise kep
d59: 📖 LEARNED: Food Preservation (Level 1). Salt, smoke, dry. The big three. Salt draws water out; bacteria can't live without it.
d59: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d59: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Owen Smith, 59 days. The mantle passes to Caleb Jones.
d59: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Caleb Jones, 35 — a Firefighter. His hands know different work now: Beast-calm, Berserker Rage.
d59: The village's quarrel was with Owen — and Owen is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d59: At the grave, Tancredi, Raj, Elif speak for Caleb — "Owen trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d59: The fire knew Caleb before the Codex did — his name already carried weight here.
